validity.researcher_notes: The McComb Compressor Station Reliability Project (Walthall County, MS) is compression-only: FERC's own Energy Infrastructure Update for December 2019 states 'Gulf South requests authorization for its McComb Compressor Station Reliability Project in Walthall County, MS, which includes installing a new 8,565 HP compressor and retiring three existing compressors. The project would result in 48 MMcf/d of increased capacity on its system' (https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/dec-energy-infrastructure.pdf, verified 200/contains 'mccomb'). The 48 MMcf/d figure matches the sheet's Capacity exactly, confirming this is the right project. No new pipeline, loop, or lateral is described anywhere in the filing record I could find — it is a compressor swap (one new unit, three retired) at an existing station, consistent with the sheet's LengthKnownKm=0.00. Per the compression-only-expansion rule (gotcha 3), the blank Diameter is the correct value, not a gap. I could not locate a second, independent (non-FERC) source describing this specific 2019 project by name (searched Federal Register, Oil & Gas Journal, Natural Gas Intel, oilandgaswatch.org — the latter's facility page for this station renders no static text via curl, JS-only); tier held at medium on that basis. The wiki's system-wide diameter string ('16 in ... 42 in') describes the whole Gulf South mainline, not this compressor-only project, and was never cited.
